I stayed for just one drink – a Long Island Iced Tea that cost about 334K, which felt really overpriced given how dead it was. Please be extremely careful if you choose to visit this establishment. Consider this a warning based on my experience.

I visited with friends and we ordered an Absolut vodka package, as it is typically our preferred drink. The drinks were brought to our table, and the server immediately opened the bottle and poured it into our glasses, mixing it with Coke for everyone except me, as I prefer mine over ice.

Helio Night Market is a fantastic choice for a family evening in Da Nang.

Both adults and kids will find something to love here. The market is clean, beautifully organized, and full of energy, with colorful lights, lively music, exciting fair-style games, and an incredible variety of delicious street food.

Children can enjoy the fun rides and games while adults relax, explore the food stalls, and soak up the vibrant atmosphere. Whether you’re looking for local specialties or international treats, there’s something for every taste. I loved wandering through the bustling stalls, trying different dishes. Helio is a fun place to spend an evening and experience Da Nang’s youthful, energetic spirit.

It’s the perfect place to laugh, eat, play, and create wonderful memories together. If you’re traveling with family, Helio Night Market is definitely a destination you shouldn’t miss.

A fantastic night market where you can enjoy not only a wide variety of food stalls but also live performances. It was great to grab some diverse food and enjoy the music performances on the stage. The location is also right near Lotte Mart, making it perfect to combine shopping with a night market visit.
Visited March 2026 and the night market is open! The place looked bright and clean, with several food & drink options. Got a delicious brown sugar milk with freshly cooked boba.

We had a really enjoyable experience at Paradise Beach Club. The place has a lovely, relaxed beachside atmosphere, making it a great spot to sit back, enjoy the surroundings and have a good meal without feeling rushed.

We ordered the Fish and Chips, and they were absolutely delicious. The fish was nicely cooked with a crispy coating, while the chips were equally enjoyable. It was simple comfort food, but done really well, and we genuinely enjoyed every bite.

The Bacon Spaghetti Carbonara was definitely the highlight of our meal. What I really liked was how generous they were with the bacon. The pasta was full of proper bacon strips, giving every bite a delicious smoky and savoury flavour. The Carbonara itself was creamy, rich and comforting, and honestly tasted exactly like it should. It was one of those dishes that you keep going back to because it is just so satisfying.

Overall, Paradise Beach Club is a great place for a relaxed meal by the beach. We loved the combination of good food, a beautiful setting and a laid-back atmosphere. Both dishes were excellent, but the Bacon Spaghetti Carbonara was definitely the one that stood out for us. I would happily visit again.

🌅🍹 ROOFTOP DA NANG – TWO VIBES, ONE FANTASTIC VENUE! 🎧💃

If you’re looking for a chilled-out rooftop bar with beautiful sea views, great drinks and a relaxed atmosphere, this place is for you.

During the day and early evening, it’s the perfect spot to unwind, catch up with friends and enjoy a few cocktails while taking in the view. The drinks are excellent, and my tip is to make the most of Happy Hour from 4–6 PM! 🍸

One of my favourite things? The music is at just the right volume. You can actually hold a conversation without having to shout over the speakers — Add friendly staff and a lovely sea breeze, and you have the perfect recipe for a relaxing afternoon.

🌅 But then sundown arrives, and the whole vibe transforms!

As daylight fades, the chilled rooftop atmosphere gives way to a livelier, high-energy party scene. The DJs take centre stage, the music turns up, and the venue becomes a place to dance the night away! 🎶🔥💃

From sunset cocktails and easy conversation to DJ beats and dancing until late — Rooftop Da Nang delivers the best of both worlds.

A beautiful setting, great drinks and two completely different experiences under one roof. Whether you're after a relaxed sundowner or a full-on night out, this place deserves a spot on your Da Nang list.

#RooftopDaNang #DaNangNightlife #HappyHour #SunsetDrinks #DJLife #VietnamNightlife #DaNangHiddenGems

The bar can be a little difficult to find if it is your first time visiting, as the sign is not very noticeable. You need to take the outdoor stairs up to the third floor, where the bar is located.

The decoration has a nice seaside theme, with wooden boards, rustic wooden barrel-style tables, and fabric panels hanging from the ceiling that gently move with the breeze, giving the place a relaxed coastal feeling. The view is definitely one of the highlights. You can enjoy the sea, especially around sunset, when the atmosphere becomes really chill and scenic.

The bar was quite lively and crowded when I visited, so it had a fun and energetic atmosphere rather than being a quiet place. I came during Happy Hour, when cocktails were 90,000 VND per glass, which I thought was a very reasonable price.

I ordered a Whiskey Sour and a Tequila Sunrise. The Whiskey Sour was refreshing, with a pleasant balance between the whiskey, citrusy sourness, and a slight sweetness. The Tequila Sunrise was smoother and fruitier, with a sweet orange flavor and a refreshing finish. Both were easy to enjoy without being too strong.

The drinks came out quickly, and the service was efficient. Overall, a fun spot for drinks, sea views, and a relaxed sunset with friends.

An extremely chill bar with music at just the right volume—you can actually have a conversation without having to shout, which is a solid 5-star plus.

The drinks are great—definitely come during happy hour from 4–6 PM. Beautiful sea view. A perfect spot to relax and hang out with friends. Friendly staff.

This is my honest review given after being request by staff:

I came here on a weekend for a solo meal (without a reservation) after being told that were no free tables at the other restaurant/bar on the other floors, so I could watch the Dragon Bridge show - a great scenic view that avoids the crowds from the main road.

Fortunately, I did not need to wait long to be seated or for my orders to come. They play western pop music and love songs (English lyrics) out loud on big speakers. The menu given digitally on a touchscreen tablet rather than in print.

I ordered the seafood spring rolls and a lobster in Cajun style (spicy) as recommended by one of the servers; it was a locally-sourced spiny lobster species, quoted 600g (medium-sized apparently), pricing being by per 100g of weight, and it comes with sliced banh mi style bread. I'm not an expert on fine dining or eating seafood but the spring rolls were tiny compared to traditional cha gio/nem ran. The lobster was somewhat underwhelming because it seemed like not all its flesh was served on my plate. I also ordered a bottle of water and a tiger beer (330ml can) as well as a shisha pipe (apple, blueberry, mint flavour) which was massive to my surprise (reminded me of massive glass pipe for a special kind of 'herb').

Anyway, if you are coming here for a special occasion like a date or with family/friends, then it's good as there is definitely a romantic vibe. The servers are friendly especially Minh Tuan and Nhu Huyen; both guys endeavoured to accommodate me as a 'viet kieu' man with less-than-fluent Vietnamese - they provided an overall positive friendly service even though we needed to communicate via Google translate.

The food itself tastes good but it let down by its actual portion size. If you are sensitive to seafood and spiciness, take caution as you may feel unwell afterwards or in the folllowing morning. The prices are quite high too for what it is, so be warned. Essentially, you are paying for an unobstructed view of the Dragon Bridge, with nice vibes, unique location and picture-esque atmosphere. If you want to save money and feel like you're getting your money's worth, then order cheaper/fewer items as you'll save a lot more because the fancy luxuries come at a premium price.

On May 22, 2026, I celebrated my birthday at a fine dining restaurant with my spouse and cousin. The food was just average, but the rooftop view was stunning, overlooking the entire Dragon Bridge and the river at sunset with perfect weather. One of the female staff members kindly helped us take photos, and she was genuinely nice and professional.

After dinner, I asked the staff to store my birthday cake in the fridge so it wouldn’t melt. Unfortunately, when we requested the cake to be served for dessert, it came out covered in ants. Clearly, the staff had failed to refrigerate it. When I pointed this out, one staff member looked flustered and couldn’t resolve the issue, so they called the shift manager. Shockingly, the manager ignored us until we insisted on his attention, and even then, he offered no solution, just played around as if it wasn’t serious.
We left the restaurant feeling extremely disappointed and angry. The lack of professionalism was unacceptable: staff had no name tags, making accountability impossible, and the team clearly lacked proper training in F&B service and hospitality. HR urgently needs to improve staff training and management standards.

reviews.text:
Vấn Cocktail Bar has a stylish, cosy interior with comfortable air conditioning and spotless facilities, including exceptionally clean restrooms, but the drinks and overall counter experience fell short.

Sitting at the counter, the hospitality felt quite distant. The bartenders and manager speak very limited English, making it tricky to discuss drink preferences or ask for recommendations. It felt as though eye contact was avoided until we actively flagged someone down, while local guests received much more attentive service.

The menu concepts look promising on paper, but the drinks lacked the complexity and strength expected at this price tier:

* Cacao: Described as one of their stronger options, but it tasted fairly mild and sweet. Decent enough, though nothing truly standout.
* Hoa Mạch: Ordered in search of a spirit forward cocktail. You get a subtle hint of the buckwheat, but the drink overall lacks body, depth, and spirit punch.
* Tomyum: Easy enough to drink and reasonably balanced, but quite standard.
* Canh Chua & Phở: Overpowered by intense chilli heat and spices. It hits you with immediate spice, but completely misses the rich, savoury, brothy depth you expect from a phở-inspired cocktail.

A major part of the craft speakeasy appeal is the bar theatre, seeing the bottles, watching the ratios, and observing how your drink is crafted. Here, most of the visible effort went into endlessly hand shaving ice, while the actual cocktail mixing happened out of sight and the drinks simply appeared. For a premium cocktail lounge in Da Nang, the execution across drink flavours and counter hospitality leaves noticeable room for improvement.

As full-time travelers behind our Sunsets & Speakeasies YouTube channel, we’re always on the hunt for cocktail bars that offer something genuinely unique. Vặn Cocktail Bar instantly earned a place among our favorites in Da Nang. From the moody lighting and sophisticated design to the carefully curated music, everything about the space feels intentional. It’s the kind of cocktail bar you settle into for the evening rather than just stopping by for one drink.

Open for around three years, Vặn is home to an exceptionally talented team of mixologists who have created one of the most creative signature menus we’ve come across in Southeast Asia. Each cocktail draws inspiration from a different Southeast Asian country, blending regional flavors into drinks that are as visually stunning as they are delicious. Every cocktail arrived looking like a miniature work of art.

The staff were incredibly knowledgeable, taking the time to explain the inspiration and ingredients behind each drink while providing attentive service throughout the evening. It’s clear they’re passionate about their craft.

We love finding bars that tell a story through their menu, and Vặn does exactly that. As the evening went on, the atmosphere became even more vibrant, and it’s easy to see why the venue fills up after 10 p.m. We visited on a Saturday, when the live DJ added another layer of energy without taking away from the intimate, upscale vibe.

One quick tip: bring cash, as the bar is currently cash only.

If you appreciate exceptional cocktails, talented mixologists, and beautifully designed spaces, Vặn Cocktail Bar is an absolute must-visit in Da Nang. Between the artistic drinks, outstanding service, and unforgettable atmosphere, it’s a bar we’ll happily return to every time we’re back in the city.
